newsitem.title: NAMIBIA: Namibia keeps ban on fx accounts for residents.
newsitem.headline: Namibia keeps ban on fx accounts for residents.

text.p: Namibia will not follow South Africa's decision to allow residents to hold foreign currency accounts, the Bank of Namibia announced.

"In the current macroeconomic environment, permitting private individuals resident in Namibia to open foreign currency accounts might exert undue pressue on the balance of payments", the bank said in a statement.
Since July 1, private individuals resident in South Africa have been able to operate foreign currency accounts with authorised dealers, or to invest abroad up to 200,000 rand.

They may retain any form of foreign income, excluding export proceeds abroad or in customer foreign currency accounts, as well as invest in fixed property such as farms or holiday houses in Southern African Development Community member countries, subject to exchange control approval.
The Bank of Namibia said it remained committed to the progressive relaxation of exchange controls.

"However, the sequence of events with regard to exchange control liberalisation should be followed with caution and with due consideration of the economic conditions prevailing at any given time", it said.
